newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money trades mostly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: German call money trades mostly unchanged.

text.p: German call money market rates traded mostly unchanged in a wide range between 3.00/3.10 percent on Thursday, unmoved after the Bundesbank drained liquidity out of the market on Wednesday.
"There were really no market moving factors today, and rates continued to trade largely steadily," a dealer said.
Traders said the decision by the Bundesbank to drain 400 million marks at the weekly tender award on Wednesday had not impacted the market significantly.
"The reserve data show that the drain did not pose any real problems for the market," another trader said.
Dealers also did not expect the Bundesbank would lower its main money market rate, the repo, which has been standing on three percent since late August at Thursday's council meeting.

On Wednesday banks held 43.2 billion marks in reserve at the Bundesbank up from 42.6 billion marks held on Tuesday. The monthly average climbed to 40.4 billion marks on Wednesday compared with 40.1 billion marks.
Borrowings at the 4.50 percent Lombard rate were neglible on Wednesday after standing at 100 million marks on Tuesday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was set at 3.08333 percent on Thursday after 3,08400 on Wednesday.
